artworks.title: Hector and Cebriones
artworks.description: Attic black-figure amphora (British Museum): Hector and Kebriones named together — Priam's bastard son as the charioteer who will fall before Patroclus in Iliad 16.

artworks.title: Hector and Cebriones (detail)
artworks.description: Closer view of the same London vase: Cebriones beside Hector — the chariot team Homer will shatter when Patroclus strikes the driver.

artworks.title: Hector and Cebriones (reverse angle)
artworks.description: Further photograph of Hector and Kebriones — Archaic clay preserving the charioteer's name centuries before Flaxman's Iliad outlines.

popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Book 16: Patroclus kills Cebriones, Hector's charioteer and half-brother — the corpse the two heroes fight over before Hector faces Achilles' friend.
